text:
A CPU branch predictor is a hardware mechanism that guesses the outcome of conditional branch instructions before the processor has fully evaluated them. Because modern CPUs use deep pipelines to execute many instructions in parallel, waiting for a branch result would create a stall. The predictor allows the processor to keep fetching and executing instructions along the path it thinks is most likely, maintaining high throughput.

Simple predictors use basic rules, such as assuming branches
